# Satsanga (Questions and Answers) | 2026 SRF World Convocation
### Speaker • Brother Kartikananda

## Opening Prayer
"Heavenly Father, Divine Mother, Friend, Beloved God, Jesus Christ, Bhagavan Krishna, Mahavatar Babaji, Lahiri Mahasaya, Swami Sri Yukteswar, Paramahansa Yogananda, saints of all religions, we bow to you all. Bless us that we may hold this satsanga with openness of heart and clarity of mind, that our questions may be rooted in sincerity and our answers rooted in thy wisdom. Om, Peace, Peace, Peace."

--- 

## Introduction
Brother Kartikananda: "Welcome, dear devotees, to this 2026 World Convocation. We gather today for Satsanga—the holy company of seekers. As our Guru, Paramahansa Yogananda, often reminded us, the questioning mind is the gateway to understanding, provided that questioning is done in the spirit of devotion. Let us begin."

--- 

### Question 1: How can I maintain a consistent meditation practice during periods of intense worldly responsibility?

Brother Kartikananda: "This is the most common challenge for the householder yogi. We often view meditation as something separate from life, but Yogananda taught that life itself is a meditation. When duties are overwhelming, do not look for an extra hour—look for the hidden moments of interiorization. Even five minutes of deep, devoted practice is superior to an hour of distracted ritual."

**Story • The Architect's Foundation**

Story: A master architect was once asked how he managed to build a cathedral while his city was under constant turmoil. He replied, 'I do not build the cathedral by focusing on the chaos in the streets. I focus on the plumb line. If the plumb line remains vertical and true, the foundation holds regardless of what happens around it.' Your meditation is your plumb line. When you are busy, focus on keeping your spine straight and your attention at the Christ Center. You will find that the work gets done with less ego-friction, and thus, less exhaustion.

--- 

### Question 2: How do I overcome the sense of loneliness that often accompanies the spiritual path?

Brother Kartikananda: "Loneliness is the ego’s way of saying it has lost its temporary identity. In the beginning, we feel apart from the world because we are stepping out of its illusions. But you are never alone. You are accompanied by the Divine, the Guru, and the entire fellowship of seekers. When you feel lonely, serve someone. In the act of selfless service, the illusion of the separate, isolated self dissolves."

**Story • The Ocean and the Wave**

Story: Yogananda often used the analogy of the wave. A wave might look at itself and feel isolated, saying, 'I am just a small, lonely wave in this vast ocean.' But when the wave settles, it realizes it was never anything but the ocean itself. Your loneliness is merely the ego trying to survive its own impending transformation. Dive deeper into the ocean of God’s presence through Kriya Yoga, and the loneliness will be replaced by the bliss of omnipresence.

--- 

## Closing Prayer
"Divine Mother, we thank Thee for this time together. Let the seeds of truth planted here today grow into the trees of realization. Help us to take the stillness of this moment back into the activity of our daily lives. Om, Peace, Peace, Peace."
